record.name: Dominican Republic
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The 2023 national AI strategy (ENIA) is run by the government ICT office and plans a permanent committee for regulatory sandboxes and a future AI law; none of its bodies tests or evaluates AI models. In September 2026 a Senate commission agreed to merge two AI bills.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English results concern the national AI strategy, development partnerships and regulation. The cached September 2026 Senate release concerns merging general AI bills for ethical/safe use and public-policy guidelines. This is not evidence of a government-designated evaluator of advanced models or an institute-specific creation study. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.governance_note: The Senate describes merging proposed AI-regulation initiatives. This establishes legislative development, not an institution to evaluate advanced models.

related_bodies.name: OGTIC and Gabinete de Innovacion y Desarrollo Digital
related_bodies.role: They lead the national AI strategy; they have no model evaluation mandate.

related_bodies.name: Comite Nacional de sandboxes regulatorios de IA (planned in ENIA)
related_bodies.role: It would assess regulatory sandboxes and regulatory options; it is not a model evaluation institute.

record.notes: The strategy PDF (primary) was read in text form. Its Objective 1.2.2 envisages a national committee to evaluate and promote regulatory sandboxes and decide the best route to regulate AI; this concerns regulation, not model evaluation. A press report seen in search results (January 2026) said about eight AI bills were pending in Congress; not opened. The Senate reported on 15 Sep 2026 that its Higher Education, Science and Technology Commission agreed to merge two bills (ethical and safe use of AI, from Senator Alexis Victoria Yeb, and public-policy guidelines for AI, from Senator Cristobal Castillo) into one. NVIDIA cooperation on an AI excellence centre and 'AI factory' was reported in search results (a presidency page) but not read.

next_check.reason: Check progress of the merged Senate AI bill (ethical and safe use of AI, merged with the AI public-policy guidelines bill) and whether it creates an AI authority.
